title: review: fix round 1: B5 v6 T-1629 new failure tests lack task ids (KeyError 'id' in full suite)
spec:
Fix round 1 for T-1629 (B5 v6, goal T-1403). Gate red 2026-10-03 15:12: the full suite errors in the two new tests in tests/test_failures.py, both with KeyError: 'id' raised from failures._rejecting_reviews (task["id"]), reached from failure_kind (the gate_red assertion at the end of test_failure_kind_incomplete_for_execute_incomplete_holds) and from failure_signature (test_failure_signature_for_incomplete_uses_head_and_dirty_set). The task dicts built in those tests have no 'id'. In the focused run no review rows existed, so the list comprehension never indexed the task; in the full suite earlier tests leave review rows in the harness bus, so it does. The production code is correct: real tasks always have an id.

Change (tests only): give every task dict built in these two tests an 'id' (a unique value no review row names, e.g. 'T-incomplete-<n>' / 'T-sig-<n>'), as the neighbouring tests in the same file do (grep '"id": "T-' there). The id is not part of the signature, so equal-signature pairs may use different ids; keep every existing assertion. Do not change any module under orchestrator/.

Verify: commit first. Then run tests/test_failures.py and tests/test_daemon.py in the foreground, then the whole tests directory once in the foreground with the same test command the gate hook uses (read .claude/hooks/tests-green.sh for it), to confirm the errors are gone under shared-bus ordering; report failures only. Never background a command. Branch: continue on task/T-1629 (head e1c4abc).
acceptance: tests/test_failures.py::test_failure_kind_incomplete_for_execute_incomplete_holds: passes: failure_kind returns 'incomplete' for hold_reason 'execute_incomplete: no commits' and for 'execute_incomplete: uncommitted changes' with an ordinary partial_output such as 'non-JSON output (rc=143): ' even when partial_output contains the word 'conflict'; returns 'quota' when partial_output contains 'usage limit reached', 'permissions' when it contains 'permission denied', 'environment' when it contains 'ModuleNotFoundError'; a hold with resume_hint missing returns 'incomplete'; existing kinds for gate_red and review holds are unchanged

tests/test_failures.py::test_failure_signature_for_incomplete_uses_head_and_dirty_set: passes: for pipeline.failure_kind 'incomplete', failure_signature differs for two holds with different resume_hint.head or different dirty sets, is equal for identical ones regardless of dirty-path order, treats a missing head as empty, and the signature of a gate_red hold is unchanged from before this change for the same input

tests/test_daemon.py::test_auto_fix_round_files_round_for_execute_incomplete_hold: passes: auto_fix_round files 'fix round 1' with fix_round_for the held id for a held task 'execute_incomplete: no commits' (pipeline.failure_kind 'incomplete', pipeline.auto_fix_route 'routine_incomplete'); a second pass files nothing; a hold whose partial_output carries a quota marker gets no round and no escalation notify; an identical second incomplete hold in the same lineage is escalated as repeated; with auto_fix_rounds 2 a third incomplete hold in the lineage gets no round; with [planner].autonomous True and routes enabled the incomplete round is still filed without calling decision.route; a task with status 'failed' and reason 'non-JSON output (rc=1): ' gets no round and no pipeline write

tests/test_daemon.py::test_fix_round_note_fences_leftovers_and_guards_missing_worktree: passes: the round spec for an incomplete hold whose worktree exists contains a data fence with the hold_reason, the head, the worktree path and each recorded dirty path, and no diff hunk; a dirty path containing three backticks cannot close the fence; partial_output appears inside the failure-text fence; when the held worktree path does not exist the note reads 'worktree: missing', says the leftovers are not recoverable and does not name the path; a gate_red round renders an empty incomplete note

result.summary: I judged this from `git diff` output, not a run. The `tests/test_failures.py` diff is the only part in scope. Its hunks do not follow the fix-round spec. The spec asks for a unique 'id' on every task dict and no other change. It also asks for a full-suite run under shared-bus ordering to confirm the errors are gone. Both new tests now stub `bus.read` to `[]`, which turns that ordering off for them. The id fix is applied incompletely. Nothing in the reviewed material shows that the two focused test files or the full suite were run.

comments.issue: `self.enterContext(patch.object(bus, "read", return_value=[]))` is added to both new tests. It hides the actual cause, which is that review rows left by earlier tests make `_rejecting_reviews` index `task['id']`. Once the stub is in, the tests no longer exercise shared-bus ordering, and the spec asked for that to be confirmed. The stub also isolates the tests from other failures that review rows would cause. The spec says to fix this by adding ids only, so the stub should be removed.

Only the gate_red dict in `test_failure_kind_incomplete_for_execute_incomplete_holds` gets an 'id'. The other dicts built in that test still have none: the 'execute_incomplete' holds in the loop and the one with resume_hint missing. They pass only because `bus.read` is stubbed. If the stub is removed, they raise KeyError: 'id' again whenever earlier tests have left review rows. The spec says every task dict in both tests needs a unique id such as 'T-incomplete-<n>'.

The `task()` helper in `test_failure_signature_for_incomplete_uses_head_and_dirty_set` gives every dict the same id, 'T-incomplete-signature'. The spec asks for unique ids that no review row names. A single fixed id is not unique, though it is probably harmless here. Separately, the gate_red check now compares against a hardcoded sha256 payload instead of the old self-equality assertion. That is a stronger assertion and fits the acceptance wording about the unchanged signature. It does tie the test to the exact JSON serialization.
